newsitem.title: USA: United Meridian extends offshore field.
newsitem.headline: United Meridian extends offshore field.

text.p: United Meridian Corporation Wednesday announced the Lion B-4 exploratory well drilled on Block CI-11 offshore the Ivory Coast extended the Lion field with a new fault block discovery.
Drilled to 12,500 feet, the B-4 has perforated a total of 170 feet in a separate reservoir compartment in the Lion sand about one mile southwest of the 1995 Lion B-3 well.

The well tested 5,360 barrels of oil and 3.4 million cubic feet of natural gas per day through a one-inch choke with 650 pound per square inch flowing tubing pressure. The Lion B-4 is expected to come on stream by the end of this week.

United Meridian said it also recently completed the Lion A-4, a field development well, which encountered almost 100 feet of net pay, including a new, deeper-pool discovery. A dual completion, the Lion A-4 tested 1,335 barrels of oil and 1.7 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the lower zone, the Foxtrot formation; the upper zone, the Senonian, was brought on production on December 13 and is producing about 3,000 barrels of oil per day. The Foxtrot sand is a new reservoir discovery in the field and the Senonian production is the first for the field.
The additional output from the Lion B-4 and A-4 will push oil production in the Lion field to well over 20,000 barrels per day, United Meridian said.

Also on Block CI-11, the Simba 1 exploratory well is currently drilling to test a Lion field look-alike prospect located four miles across a shallow syncline to the west of the Lion field. Simba's target is the same fault block encountered in the Lion B-3 well, which contained 450 feet of gross pay in the Albian sand. The well is expected to reach total depth by the end of December.

United Meridian, the operator, holds a 25-percent interest in Block CI-11. Partners in the Block include PETROCI, the Ivory Coast's national oil company, with 40 percent; International Finance Corporation with 15 percent; and Pluspetrol SA and Seagull Energy Corp with 10 percent each.
The rig currently drilling Simba is expected to move to Block CI-01 in January to commence drilling on the Kudu prospect in which United Meriidian has a 45 percent interest, the company said.

The Kudu 1 will attempt to extend the field's proven natural gas reserves and increase the upside potential of the field, United said. Current proven reserves are scheduled to meet the initial gas demands in Abidjan, the capitol of Cote d'Ivoire, and in the neighboring country to the east, Ghana.

But new-found reserves would be available to meet increasing demand generated by both countries' expanding economies, the company said, noting natural gas sales contracts are currently under negotiation with each country. With an approved contract, first natural gas sales could commence in the second half of 1998.
United's partners in Block CI-01 are PETROCI, with 40 percent, and Yukong Ltd with 15 percent.
